keep running?
question.source: the user, approved 2026-09-27 (docs/research/2026-09-27-codex-rewrite-options.md#48): a shared resource that needs maintenance and outlasts the people around it; shortened from 'What do you help keep in working order?', which ran off the frame (8 words, 22-character line; the rules allow 6 and 18)

caption.text: The town changes; the well doesn’t, and the water is always there. What fails is a rope that’s too short or a bucket that breaks.

lesson.text:
Mend it.
Share it.

ONCE THE CHANGE IS TRUSTED,
STOP PUSHING.

hook.text: Got the ingredients, not the result?

meaning.text:
The Caldron says:
set it right.

A tilted pot
spills the meal.

question.text:
What’s out of
place right now?

caption.text: Wood feeds the fire under the caldron. In its worst line a leg snaps and the duke’s stew spills: a load too heavy for what holds it up.

lesson.text:
Set the pot firm,
then cook.
lesson.source: series/characters.json#50: The legs rise; a fire is lit among them; the bowl, drawn high above, drops onto them.

meaning.text:
The Arousing says:
use the fear.

Let it show
what to fix.

question.text:
What did the
scare show you?

caption.text: The image is thunder, twice. You scream, then you laugh, and your hands still don’t drop the cup. A good scare is a chance to put things in order.

lesson.text:
When shaken,
examine yourself.
lesson.source: Image on 51: 恐懼修省 (uses fear and trembling to examine themselves)

name: Keeping Still
commentary: Still the back — not the front.

music.title: 80s Retro Inspiring Synth Pop by DIMMYSAD
music.licence: Pixabay Content License, Content ID registered

meaning.text:
Stay with where
you are now.

caption.text: The old text says to keep your back still, so you stop chasing what’s in front of you.

lesson.text:
Stop when it's
time to stop.

readout.finding: NO PAIR ANSWERS. EACH STANDS STILL.

lesson.readout_source: image: thinks of nothing beyond the present situation

Development says:
go step by step.

Do the work
at each step.

caption.text: A tree on a mountain grows where everyone can see it. Build the character you want others to learn from.

lesson.text:
Earn each place
before the next.

LINES 2–5 EACH HOLD THEIR PLACE.

meaning.text:
Marrying Maiden
says: see the end.

question.text:
What does the
end look like?

caption.text: The old image is a young bride who arrives while the first wife still runs the house. She goes back and waits her turn; the text warns against pushing ahead.

lesson.text:
Wrong place?
Don't push.

readout.finding: LINES 2 TO 5 ALL OUT OF PLACE.

caption.text: Noon is when the sun starts to sink, and the text still says don’t worry. Waste noon worrying about the afternoon and you never have a noon.

lesson.text:
At your fullest,
light each corner.

readout.finding: THUNDER AND FIRE AT ONCE: FULL.

hook.text: Somewhere new, feeling out of place?

meaning.text:
You’re a guest.
Act like one.

caption.text: In the old text, a traveler who plays the host loses the inn to fire and the servants with it. Fire on a mountain moves on, and so does a guest.

lesson.text:
Play the host,
risk your room.

name: The Gentle
commentary: Small fulfillment again — the gentle force doesn't produce dramatic results.

music.title: Retro Synth Pop by AliveTunes

meaning.text:
The Gentle says:
say it again.

caption.text: Wind follows wind. Wang Bi says to repeat an instruction before and after it takes effect, giving people time to change.

lesson.text:
People change slowly.
Say it again, gently.
lesson.source: series/critic/depth/review.json#57; Great Image 君子以申命行事 (the noble one repeats the charge and carries out affairs); the user, 2026-09-28: 'sure fix them' (after 49 and 46: 'i like what your reviewers proposed vs now. the current wording is a bit dense/confusing'); Codex's review agrees (docs/research/2026-09-27-codex-rewrite-options.md)

readout.finding:
LINE 5: SAY IT, THEN AGAIN.
PEOPLE CAN'T CHANGE AT ONCE.

lesson.readout_source: 九五 先庚三日，後庚三日 (three days before, three days after); Wang Bi 以正齊物，不可卒也 (setting people right can't be done all at once)

hook.text: Good news, no one to tell?

caption.text: Two lakes together: friends talking and learning from each other. Enjoy the company without pretending to agree.

lesson.text:
Laugh and learn
with friends.
lesson.source: series/characters.json#58: A figure's mouth rises open; the two lines above it lift out of it and float, bobbing, like laughter.

commentary: The king goes to the temple.

meaning.text:
Remind them where
they come from.

caption.text: Wind over water scatters the surface, so the old kings built temples: a place everyone comes back to, around what they hold in common.

lesson.text:
Bring them back
to what they share.

readout.finding:
LINE 5: THE KING SENDS OUT HIS CALL.
RIGHTLY PLACED AT THE CENTRE.

lesson.readout_source: judgment: the king approaches the temple

name: Limitation
commentary: Limitation brings fulfillment — but bitter limitation breaks.

music.title: Synthwave by EvgeniaCh
music.licence: Pixabay Content License, Content ID registered

caption.text: A lake holds only so much water, and that’s what makes it a lake. Limits work; harsh limits break.

lesson.text:
Set limits
you can keep.
lesson.source: series/critic/depth/review.json#60; Judgment 苦節不可貞 (bitter limits can't be kept); the user, 2026-09-28: 'sure fix them' (after 49 and 46: 'i like what your reviewers proposed vs now. the current wording is a bit dense/confusing'); Codex's review agrees (docs/research/2026-09-27-codex-rewrite-options.md)

readout.finding:
LINE 5: A SWEET LIMIT.
IT KEEPS TO THE MIDDLE.

lesson.readout_source: 九五 甘節，吉 (a sweet limit, good); Small Image 居位中也 (it keeps to the middle); Wang Bi 為節而不苦 (a limit that isn't bitter). Line 5 is Wang Bi's master, so the master stays.

commentary: Piglets and fish — the least spiritual, least intelligent creatures available.

meaning.text:
Hold off judging
until you do.

question.text:
What haven’t you
asked them yet?

caption.text: The old text says trust reaches even pigs and fishes. It also asks judges to examine a case carefully before taking a life.

lesson.text:
Make room
to hear them.

The Small says:
no big moves.

question.text:
What small thing
can you do?

lesson.text:
Fly low.
Do small things.

Done? Now guard
against trouble.

meaning.text:
Sort things out
before you move.

caption.text: The book’s last hexagram is a little fox that gets its tail wet just before the far bank. Sixty-four hexagrams, and the last word is: not yet.

lesson.text:
Almost done?
Stay careful to the end.
